applicability: Problem A tasks asking where, when, or under what geometry performance is maximized
forbidden: Naming an optimum from intuition
Calling a final-speed maximum a COR maximum when COR is fixed
Equating comfort and power without a decision model
Ignoring a quadratic root or boundary
Treating one operating condition as universal
inapplicable: Tasks where no defensible scalar metric exists without stakeholder tradeoffs
positive_pattern: Batted-ball speed is derived over impact location, its interior maximum is compared with the tip and center of percussion, and operating-condition dependence is reported.
procedure: Separate competing definitions of the named feature.
Choose a physically meaningful response metric.
Derive the metric from governing relations.
Differentiate or numerically optimize over the target variable.
Name the optimized response rather than a fixed input parameter.
Check all roots, stationary points, and boundaries.
Sweep uncertain operating inputs.
Report the optimum, a physical tolerance, and movement across regimes.
statement: Define the named physical feature as an optimizer of an explicit, unit-bearing performance function over the relevant spatial or operating variable.

applicability: Reduced collision, vibration, or transport models where full transient simulation is unnecessary
forbidden: Hiding arbitrary correction factors
Calling an unvalidated coefficient physical
Combining mutually incompatible scale assumptions
Omitting regime limits
inapplicable: Cases where the effective parameter cannot be calibrated or changes unpredictably across the domain
positive_pattern: A rigid collision supplies intuition, its instantaneous-whole-body assumption is rejected by a contact-time comparison, and the omitted wave mechanism is then modeled or bounded.
procedure: State the omitted mechanism and compare its time and length scales with the retained process.
Define the effective parameter from conservation or energy relations.
Identify its component material or structural parameters.
Calibrate against regime-matched measurements.
Check the omitted mechanism near the predicted optimum.
Bound the remaining error and name when the reduction fails.
statement: Use an effective physical parameter or reduced model to compress omitted fast dynamics only when its components retain physical meaning and the omitted mechanism is revisited at the operating point.

applicability: Comparisons of materials, structures, or technologies with many confounding mechanical properties
forbidden: Calling a compound geometry-mass-stiffness comparison a material effect
Comparing commercial examples with uncontrolled differences
Generalizing directly from one special matched case
inapplicable: Cases where matching constraints are infeasible or erase the mechanism of interest
positive_pattern: A theoretical aluminum bat is matched to wood on mass, center of mass, inertia, length, and outline before trampoline behavior is compared.
procedure: State whether the estimand is material alone or a real product class.
List confounding properties.
Construct a feasible comparator matched on those properties.
Vary only the target mechanism.
Compare outputs.
Then relax matching constraints one at a time.
Validate manufacturing and operational feasibility.
statement: Isolate a material or technology effect with a matched-property counterfactual before generalizing across real designs.

applicability: Coupled physical models with empirical parameter relationships
forbidden: Claiming exact agreement from similar curves
Using one-factor sweeps as full robustness proof
Ignoring empirical-fit uncertainty
Reporting Monte Carlo bounds without reproducible inputs and convergence checks
inapplicable: Monotone analytic relationships with proven signs and no coupled inputs
positive_pattern: The 2010 paper identifies indeterminate inertia/mass effects and performs bounded sweeps; the 2025 paper demonstrates why local propagation, undocumented Monte Carlo, and one-factor plots are insufficient as robustness evidence.
procedure: Draw the dependency paths.
Mark competing signs.
Define plausible ranges, distributions, and dependencies.
Run one-factor sweeps for interpretation.
Run joint/global sensitivity for robustness.
Check decision stability, not only output movement.
Compare against external data with residuals and uncertainty.
statement: When direct and indirect parameter effects oppose each other, replace sign-only reasoning with bounded simulation, joint uncertainty analysis, and quantitative external error metrics.

forbidden: Leaving prohibition questions out of the objectives then answering them ad hoc
Orphan computations
Silently narrowing the official objective
Conclusions introducing unmodeled material or policy claims
Treating an opening workflow as proof of completed coverage
positive_pattern: A complete paper lists each task, assigns a model and validation, and closes in order; qualitative policy hypotheses are visibly separated from mechanics output.
procedure: Enumerate official tasks in the introduction, including policy questions.
Group related tasks without deleting deliverables.
Preview the model assigned to each task.
Name intermediate outputs and dependencies.
Present results in task order or provide explicit handoffs.
Audit measurement and policy constraints as requirements.
Close the conclusion in original task order with answers, evidence class, and uncertainty.
statement: Maintain a requirement trace from each official subquestion through its model, output, verification, and final answer.

forbidden: Unlabeled 3D perspective
Using agreement with the target outcome to define the feasible region
No plan or contour view
No baseline
Hidden fixed parameters
A fitted surface without calibration, residuals, or uncertainty
inapplicable: Sparse observations
Categorical inputs
Surfaces with severe interpolation uncertainty
Uncalibrated image intensities presented as physical depth
positive_pattern: A pitch-speed and swing-speed surface is paired with a unit-labeled contour map whose feasible region and held-out observed sweet-spot error are directly marked.
procedure: Compute a gridded response with units.
Plot a surface for global shape.
Plot readable contours or an aligned plan view.
Mark the baseline, optimum, feasible region, and decision boundary.
Keep validation targets separate from constraints used to create the mask.
Use a perceptually ordered palette.
State fixed parameters and calibration.
Add residual and uncertainty views when fitted.
statement: For a two-variable physical design or operating space, pair a response surface with a labeled plan or contour view and mark the baseline, feasible region, and decision boundary directly.

forbidden: Calling a 1.41 percent absolute speed increase a 145 percent speed improvement
Reversing a result because an unmodeled effect might dominate
Exactly matches without residuals
Ideal model despite blocking closure errors
Prose direction opposite to formula or figure
positive_pattern: Results are scannable with numerical answers and candid limits, while percentages name their denominator and omitted mechanisms do not reverse the stated result without evidence.
procedure: Name the metric, numerator, denominator, and comparison.
Report the numerical result and uncertainty.
State scope, dataset, and evaluation split.
Reconcile equations, figures, and prose direction.
Use agreement language calibrated to error.
For innovation or causality, name the baseline, mechanism, and measured gain.
Move unsupported counterfactual or policy language to a hypothesis.
statement: Write quantitative abstract, validation, and innovation claims at the strength supported by the metric; reserve exact, proves, verified, reliable, ideal, and causal wording for explicit comparative evidence.

applicability: Problem A physical models that end in regulation, design, or stakeholder recommendations
forbidden: Presenting fairness or tradition as an equation output
Calling easier swing an unfair advantage without behavioral evidence
Using a small speed difference as injury proof
Treating a null performance difference as a ban explanation
Rhetorical historical harm without a scoring or stakeholder model
positive_pattern: The analysis separately traces speed and control through reaction, injury, fairness, tradition, enforceability, and stakeholder criteria before recommending a rule.
procedure: List direct physical outputs.
Translate outputs into exposure or performance consequences.
Introduce stakeholder risk or value criteria.
State normative and institutional assumptions.
Model behavioral claims such as decision time or contact accuracy.
Compare enforceability and alternative rules.
Test thresholds and uncertainty.
Qualify the recommendation and answer every policy question.
statement: Separate mechanical model outputs from safety, fairness, tradition, and policy value judgments, then state and test the bridge assumptions explicitly.

applicability: Images converted to depth, wear, deformation, temperature, pressure, or concentration fields
forbidden: Treating grayscale or probability density as metric depth
Selecting the best-looking sample after processing
Omitting source provenance
Reporting more digits than measurement resolution supports
inapplicable: Images used only as qualitative context with no quantitative physical claim
positive_pattern: A field-ready stair study would pair calibrated scans with scale targets, repeat registration, depth residuals, and an uncertainty map before inferring traffic or age.
procedure: Document source provenance, acquisition geometry, and sensor settings.
Place physical scale and reference targets in the scene.
Correct perspective, lens distortion, registration, and illumination effects.
Repeat acquisitions and quantify repeatability.
Validate recovered values against a known physical reference.
Report units, resolution, detection limit, and spatial uncertainty.
Propagate the uncertainty into fitted parameters and final decisions.
statement: Calibrate every image-derived physical field before it enters a forward or inverse model, and carry measurement uncertainty through all downstream results.

forbidden: Inverting one wear snapshot for several unknown causes
Calling a friction coefficient a wear coefficient
Treating disagreement between separate estimators as proof of renovation
Assuming a temporal-use mechanism below sensor resolution
inapplicable: Forward prediction with all influential parameters independently measured
positive_pattern: A stair-wear model would jointly estimate traffic history and renovation change points from multiple calibrated steps while measuring material properties separately.
procedure: Write the forward damage model and units.
List all latent factors that can produce the same observation.
Build a parameter-to-observation dependency graph.
Test structural identifiability analytically or with profile likelihood.
Use multiple sites, times, materials, or independent sensors to break confounding.
Fit one coherent model for age, load history, material, environment, and interventions.
Run synthetic-recovery and change-point tests.
Report equivalence classes or bounds when unique recovery is impossible.
statement: Before inverting accumulated physical damage for age, traffic, or event history, establish which latent factors are identifiable from the available observations and add independent measurements for confounded factors.

forbidden: Dimensionally incomplete inertia or force terms
Calling continuity alone Navier-Stokes
Omitting constitutive or velocity closure
Reporting a PDE without grid or time-step convergence
Ignoring a plot/prose scale conflict
Applying arbitrary output thresholds
inapplicable: Sparse individual behavior where a discrete agent model is the natural observational scale
positive_pattern: A transient beam-impact model declares rho A, point-load coupling, free and fixed boundary conditions, contact law, grid and integrator, then passes impulse, energy, mesh, and experimental checks.
procedure: Define state variables and physical units.
Justify the continuum scale.
State every conservation law and constitutive closure, including mass or linear density and load units.
Specify initial, boundary, contact, and source conditions.
Choose a discretization and derive its stability condition.
Check conservation, convergence, and limiting cases.
Calibrate against regime-matched fields or trajectories.
Define and validate the rule that maps simulation output to the final decision.
statement: Use a continuum or PDE model only after specifying a dimensionally complete governing closure, initial and boundary conditions, numerical stability and convergence, and a validated mapping from field output to the requested behavior.

applicability: All Problem A model validation sections
forbidden: Defining model applicability by requiring its prediction to match the accepted answer
Calling range inclusion accuracy
Calling internal agreement external validation
Claiming transferred assumptions are experimentally verified by precedent alone
Using known context as a circular check
positive_pattern: A predicted sweet-spot location is scored against held-out measured locations with error bars after conservation and root checks, rather than declared valid because scenarios outside the accepted range are masked away.
procedure: List each target claim and its required evidence.
Use conservation, ablations, boundary counterfactuals, and limiting cases internally.
Use observed ranges only as held-out scoring targets, not filters that define applicability.
Use residual plots for fit diagnostics.
Use synthetic data to test recovery.
Use regime-matched external data for empirical validation.
Reserve a genuine holdout or blind case.
Set thresholds from resolution or operational loss.
Report failure cases and uncertainty.
statement: Separate internal mechanism checks, plausibility ranges, synthetic recovery, regime-matched external comparison, and true holdout validation; label each by the claim it can and cannot support.

forbidden: Declaring consistency in one section and contradiction in the next
Using estimator disagreement as proof without a null discrepancy distribution
Ignoring shared coefficient and calibration errors
inapplicable: Independent estimators intentionally reported as unresolved alternatives
positive_pattern: A renovation conclusion would follow from a shared likelihood whose no-repair model cannot explain both calibrated wear and historical age within uncertainty.
procedure: Place every estimator in one dependency graph.
Align definitions, units, time windows, and conditioning assumptions.
Propagate shared measurement and parameter uncertainty.
Compute the expected discrepancy under a no-change model.
Compare alternative explanations for the discrepancy.
Introduce a repair or change-point parameter in the shared model.
Report evidence for change relative to calibrated alternatives.
statement: Reconcile multiple estimates of the same physical quantity inside one model before interpreting their disagreement as repair, anomaly, or mechanism change.

forbidden: A model surface without its source field
Implicit normalization
Radar area treated as similarity
Heatmap values inconsistent with prose
Decorative 3D perspective without residuals
inapplicable: Purely schematic figures with no quantitative evidentiary role
positive_pattern: A stair-wear figure chain would show the source photograph, calibrated depth map, bivariate fit, residual map, uncertainty map, and the exact region integrated for traffic inference.
procedure: Show the uncropped or traceably cropped source with physical scale.
Show the calibrated measured field with units and a perceptually ordered color scale.
Show the fitted or simulated field on aligned coordinates and identical limits.
Show signed and absolute residual fields.
Show uncertainty or detection-limit overlays.
Mark the region, threshold, or statistic used for the final decision.
Reconcile every chart scale with values reported in text and tables.
State transformations and normalization in the caption.
statement: For a physical field derived from images or scans, visualize the full evidence chain from source through calibration and fit to residuals, uncertainty, and the final decision.

forbidden: Equal weights by convenience called universal
Unexplained comfort scaling
Design-specific min-max scores compared directly
Arbitrary objective threshold
Preference shift called stable without tolerance
Zone width used as behavioral proof
inapplicable: A single universally accepted physical optimum
positive_pattern: Exit speed, grip impulse, vibration, and control are measured on common scales; player preferences select a Pareto point and a validated loss tolerance defines the sweet zone.
procedure: Define each objective in physical units and its measured outcome.
Calibrate any comfort or control proxy.
Choose normalization from common reference ranges rather than each design's extrema.
Elicit or scenario-test preference weights.
Plot the Pareto frontier and optima over preference scenarios.
Define a tolerance zone from decision loss or empirical variability.
Compare designs on the same objective scales and thresholds.
statement: Define a physical sweet spot or operating zone as a transparent multi-objective decision over unit-bearing performance, comfort, control, and safety, with calibrated normalization, elicited preferences, Pareto tradeoffs, and common cross-design tolerances.

forbidden: Setting final bat translation and rotation both to zero while claiming conservation
Using pivot inertia in a center-of-mass free-bat formula
Force equated directly to acceleration
Grip acceleration called comfort without validation
Rigid pivot used without external impulse
No sign, root, recoil, or limiting-case test
inapplicable: Static equipment geometry with no collision claim
positive_pattern: A measured collision pulse drives a model whose ball impulse, bat translation and rotation, wave return, center-of-percussion response, grip force, and energy loss close in one reference frame and match tests.
procedure: Declare an inertial frame, origins, axes, velocity signs, and pre-impact states.
Choose free-bat or constrained-grip dynamics and include the corresponding external impulse.
Write linear and angular impulse balances about one declared reference and translate all inertias consistently.
Retain and solve post-impact bat translation and rotation.
Use a physically defined restitution or compliant-contact model.
Compare contact duration with wave and support return times.
Verify energy, momentum, root, and physical bounds.
Validate exit speed, recoil, grip load, contact pulse, and vibration.
statement: Build bat-ball impact models from consistent frames, impulse, angular momentum, compliant contact, grip boundary, and vibration mechanics, preserving recoil states, mass factors, signs, units, contact duration, and the distinction between center-of-percussion response and hand load.

forbidden: Calling departure speed divided by pitch speed COR
Calling a speed ratio an energy fraction
Substituting unknown final speed into e and then predicting that same speed
Undefined bat contact velocity
Implied e above one without an energy source
Material curve created only by scaling another fit
inapplicable: Purely elastic symbolic derivations with e fixed by premise
positive_pattern: Matched wood and metal impacts use local relative approach and separation speeds, independently calibrated bounded COR, and held-out exit-speed validation while reporting BESR separately.
procedure: Write a definition crosswalk for COR, apparent COR, BESR or BBCOR, and energy return.
Declare the reference frame and local pre- and post-contact velocities.
Measure or independently calibrate the coefficient before predicting exit speed.
Publish raw impacts, designs, conditions, and uncertainty.
Fit constrained models and inspect residuals.
Enforce physical and energy bounds.
Reconcile every material baseline.
Validate against held-out exit speed.
statement: Define and calibrate restitution or effective collision efficiency from compatible relative velocities and target-specific measurements; distinguish it from certification speed ratios and energy fractions, preserve bounds, and never infer it from the outcome it is meant to predict.

forbidden: Negative parallel-axis shift for total original mass
Removed mass distance measured from the wrong center
Jo used for center inertia
Multiple untracked axis translations
No zero-removal recovery
Mass and inertia tables with inconsistent labels
inapplicable: Unchanged rigid bodies with directly measured inertia
positive_pattern: Removing a cylindrical core gives identical remaining inertia from direct integration and pivot-axis subtraction followed by one positive parallel-axis shift to the new center.
procedure: Declare every component mass, centroid, own-axis inertia, and sign as added or removed.
Compute total mass and first moment.
Compute inertia about a fixed reference axis by addition and subtraction.
Translate once to the new center using the parallel-axis theorem.
Cross-check by direct integration or a second reference-axis calculation.
Test zero modification and full-domain limits.
Label center and pivot inertias unambiguously.
statement: Compute mass, center of mass, and inertia changes for removed, added, or redistributed material from one declared reference axis and verify first-moment and parallel-axis identities before using them in dynamics.

forbidden: Hand-selecting 35.791, 36.5, and 38 rad/s without a fitted relation
Using undefined linear bat speed alongside angular speed
Mass-speed coupling applied inconsistently
Easier swing asserted to improve contact without data
One batter capability assumed universal
One-factor partial derivative called product advice
inapplicable: Machine-driven impact at controlled speed
positive_pattern: A player-specific model jointly predicts center translation, angular speed, local barrel speed, contact dispersion, decision time, exit speed, and fatigue across matched bats.
procedure: Choose player groups and measured capability distributions.
Estimate the joint relationship among mass, inertia, balance, geometry, center-of-mass translation, and angular kinematics.
Combine translation and rotation into local contact velocity in one frame.
Model contact-location accuracy, timing, and decision time as outcomes.
Propagate fatigue and repeated-swing effects.
Use one matched coupling model across cork, wood, and metal.
Validate against player and batted-ball data.
statement: Evaluate equipment mass, balance, material, and geometry jointly with achievable human motion, contact accuracy, decision time, fatigue, strength, and player heterogeneity rather than assigning or varying swing speed independently.

forbidden: Representing corking only by assumed mass, inertia, and hand-picked swing speed
Replacing the filled cavity by a hollow barrel
Filler or cap omitted
Incorrect remaining inertia
Unmodeled energy loss used to reverse a result
Contact or decision-time advantage asserted without evidence
Ban explained only by speculation
inapplicable: Pure mass-removal demonstrations
positive_pattern: Actual corked and matched legal bats are tested and modeled for mass, compliance, exit speed, vibration, contact, strength, and policy consequences.
procedure: Specify actual cavity diameter, depth, cap, filler, density, stiffness, damping, and bond.
Recompute mass, center, and inertia with invariant tests.
Estimate player-specific swing, contact, and decision-time response.
Model local compliance, restitution, vibration, and failure.
Compare legal uncorked, mass-matched, inertia-matched, hollow-only, and actual corked designs.
Measure exit speed, dispersion, grip response, durability, and uncertainty.
Separate physics from enforceability, deception, fairness, and safety policy.
statement: Model corking as a complete structural, human, and collision modification including removed wood, filler and cap mass, stiffness, damping, bonding, cavity geometry, strength, swing coupling, and rule-relevant counterfactuals before concluding performance or prohibition effects.

forbidden: Concluding material matters from a model with no material variable
Creating the metal advantage only by assumed inertia and swing speed
Compound product comparison called material isolation
Unmodeled trampoline effect added rhetorically to a numerical result
Frequency-only hoop surrogate
No real-product validation
inapplicable: Same-material parameter tuning
positive_pattern: Wood and metal are compared as matched specimens and legal products with measured material properties, swing, contact pulse, hoop response, exit speed, durability, and risk.
procedure: Define whether the estimand is material or a product bundle.
Construct geometry-, mass-, inertia-, and performance-matched counterfactuals where feasible.
Include at least one measured material property in a claimed material mechanism.
Use compatible measured contact and damping data.
Apply one human swing model.
Model thickness-dependent structure, waves, hoop modes, damping, and restitution.
Compare on common scales and uncertainty.
Connect outputs to validated safety and fairness outcomes.
statement: Compare bat materials through feasible matched and real-design counterfactuals that jointly represent geometry, mass, balance, swing response, stiffness, damping, wave propagation, barrel compliance, restitution, strength, standards, and common performance and safety metrics.

forbidden: Calling 0.756 m/s enough to be dangerous without a risk model
Adding an unmodeled trampoline effect to strengthen a safety claim
Exit speed alone called injury proof
No exposure or reaction model
Safety threshold without evidence
inapplicable: Performance analysis making no safety claim
positive_pattern: Measured exit distributions feed pitcher and infielder injury-risk models across trajectories, reaction distances, exposures, and protection, with uncertainty and a wood baseline.
procedure: Define the exposed person, hazard, contact pathway, and injury endpoint.
Compute full impulse and bat response.
Use measured contact histories.
For fielders, combine exit-speed and direction distributions, flight, distance, reaction, protection, and exposure.
Compare risk against a baseline, not just speed difference.
Calibrate injury thresholds and uncertainty.
Compare policy alternatives.
statement: Translate equipment mechanics into safety only through validated impulse, contact, flight, exposure, reaction-time, injury, and uncertainty models; never infer hand or fielder injury from exit speed or an incomplete force quotient alone.

forbidden: One-factor plots after admitting variables are coupled
Hand-selected swing speeds treated as data
Sensitivity of a circular or undefined equation
Mass varied with swing speed fixed
No structural uncertainty
No recommendation reversal
inapplicable: Exact identities with no uncertain input
positive_pattern: Global analysis jointly varies player capability, bat geometry, restitution, local contact velocity, material, and model closure and reports location and policy reversals.
procedure: Create an uncertainty and structural-alternative register.
Define joint feasible distributions and correlations.
Include measurements, fitted contact laws, geometry, human response, and material properties.
Resolve undefined or hand-selected variables before sensitivity.
Use screening and global interaction-aware methods.
Reoptimize in every scenario.
Report optimum movement, performance, feasibility, and policy reversal.
Prioritize measurements by decision value.
statement: Use global, coupled, and decision-centered sensitivity for physical design models, reporting output ranges, interactions, closure uncertainty, feasibility, and recommendation reversals rather than only one-at-a-time local sweeps.

forbidden: Undefined V_i
Unreported coordinate needed to convert d to knob location
Outcome used to define its own e
No code or calculator file
Percentage denominator unnamed
Citation title and URL disagree
Narrative direction differs from formula
inapplicable: Pure analytic proof with no numerical result
positive_pattern: One command rebuilds COP and power locations, independently calibrated exit speeds, cork and material scenarios, sensitivity maps, percentages, citations, and a clean PDF while frame, conservation, root, and text-figure checks pass.
procedure: Archive primary data and definitions.
Provide geometry, absolute and relative coordinates, units, component ledgers, code, software versions, solver or calculator settings, and root choices.
Record every independent calibration parameter.
Add dimensional, frame, inertia, impulse, energy, sign, bound, and percentage tests.
Regenerate every optimum, scenario, table, and figure.
Compare equations, labels, values, percentages, and narrative automatically.
Validate citation title-URL pairs and PDF links.
Fail release on unexplained mismatch.
statement: Publish and test an end-to-end reproduction path for Problem A geometry, coordinate systems, governing equations, fitted laws, collision calculations, optimizations, sensitivity figures, tables, citations, and document export.

forbidden: Selecting modes only by low natural frequency
Treating a short contact as both perfectly rigid and spatially local
Assuming a real grip is exactly free or fixed
Using boundary nodes without a return-time argument
Calling a transient mechanism validated without measured timing
inapplicable: Quasistatic loading where the whole structure equilibrates during forcing
positive_pattern: A 1.4 ms contact pulse is compared with space-time wave traces; free and fixed boundary counterfactuals and a long-domain limit show which reflections can change exit speed.
procedure: Measure or estimate the contact-force time history.
Compute wave speeds for each relevant mode and material region.
Map travel and return times from the contact point to tapers, ends, grips, and interfaces.
Model free, fixed, and impedance boundary alternatives.
Retain only signals that return while contact can exchange energy.
Check rigid-body and long-domain limiting cases.
Validate transient displacement, force, and exit response at multiple locations.
statement: For short-duration structural impact, determine locality and boundary influence by comparing contact duration with wave travel, reflection, and return times through the actual geometry and support impedance.

forbidden: Writing acceleration equal to force
Using volumetric density where linear density is required
Publishing only a continuum equation or only code
No grid or time-step convergence
Unreported unloading branch or event switch
Typesetting ambiguity treated as harmless without code
inapplicable: Closed-form models with no numerical discretization
positive_pattern: A ball-beam solver closes equal-and-opposite contact force, impulse, rigid modes, and hysteretic energy loss while exit speed and contact duration converge under grid refinement.
procedure: Write a unit table for every state, load, density, stiffness, and derivative.
Derive the discrete equations from segment or control-volume balances.
Check that each force is divided by the correct mass and applied with equal and opposite signs.
Publish grid, time step, integrator, tolerances, and event handling.
Test free and fixed ghost or boundary equations against analytic modes.
Monitor momentum and energy including modeled hysteretic loss.
Repeat on refined grids and time steps.
Compare with an independent implementation or benchmark.
statement: Before trusting a coupled transient PDE/ODE simulation, make every term dimensionally consistent and verify force-mass coupling, boundary implementation, conservation, stability, and spatial and temporal convergence.

forbidden: Assuming Euclidean orthogonality without the mass matrix
Discarding high modes only because their frequency is high
Repeating cosine for both Fourier phase families
Specifying a surrogate oscillator by frequency alone
Equating contact duration directly with resonance frequency
No full-model or experimental comparison
inapplicable: Direct spatial solvers where no modal truncation is used
positive_pattern: A shell-contact model uses biorthogonal or mass-normalized modes, reports modal impedance and damping, retains modes until the contact-force response converges, and matches measured hoop spectra.
procedure: Form the generalized mass and stiffness operators.
Determine whether the operator is self-adjoint, generalized symmetric, or non-normal.
Project forcing with the mass-weighted or left-eigenvector basis.
Include both sine and cosine azimuthal phases when symmetry does not remove one.
Compute modal mass, stiffness, damping, and contact participation.
Select modes from the force spectrum and convergence, not frequency rank alone.
Validate reduced transients against the full model and measured frequency response.
statement: Use modal reduction only with the correct mass or energy inner product or a biorthogonal left-right basis, and calibrate each retained mode by modal mass, stiffness, damping, contact coupling, and excitation spectrum.

forbidden: Only an animation still with no time marker
Removing rigid motion without disclosure
Seven color-only curves identified by caption order
No baseline or optimum marker
Transient picture used as quantitative validation
inapplicable: Static scalar calculations with no temporal mechanism
positive_pattern: A force-time plot establishes 1.4 ms contact, aligned bat snapshots show whether a reflected pulse returns, and labeled response curves show how that return moves the exit-speed optimum.
procedure: Plot the contact force and mark contact start, peak, reversal, and release.
Show aligned deformation snapshots or a space-time field with rigid motion and other transformations disclosed.
Overlay the baseline and one mechanism or boundary change at a time.
Connect the transient difference to the response-versus-decision-variable curve.
Mark optima, tolerances, and uncertainty.
Use direct labels and line-style redundancy for grayscale and color-vision accessibility.
statement: Explain a transient physical mechanism with a linked visual chain of contact force over time, space-time deformation, boundary or mechanism counterfactuals, and the final response curve on common units and highlighted decision points.

forbidden: Calling b distance from the hand pivot in a center-of-mass free-bat formula
Using pivot inertia while omitting center translation
Adding a six-inch pivot offset without publishing the center coordinate
Treating local bat speed, center speed, and angular speed as independent
Conserving linear momentum for a constrained pivot without support impulse
inapplicable: Pure translation with no moment or reference-axis dependence
positive_pattern: A free-bat solution uses center-of-mass inertia and contact offset, retains center translation and rotation, then converts the optimum to distance from the knob with a published coordinate ledger and reproduces it from a pivot-frame calculation including support impulse.
procedure: Draw the origin, center of mass, pivot or grip, contact point, and positive axes.
State whether the body is free or externally constrained during contact.
Define every linear velocity at its physical point and combine center translation with omega cross r.
Write angular momentum about a fixed inertial point or the center of mass.
Use inertia about that same point or apply the parallel-axis theorem once.
Include support impulse when a pivot is constrained.
Transform reported optima to field coordinates through an explicit coordinate ledger.
Verify the result in a second reference frame.
statement: Close rigid-body impact in one declared inertial frame and transform impact offsets, centers of mass, translational velocities, angular velocities, and inertias together whenever the reference point changes.

forbidden: Undefined V_i
Using v_f to define e and then claiming to predict v_f
Setting recoil velocities to zero while retaining recoil terms
Implied superelastic e without an energy source
Calling a parameter-bundle comparison a material prediction
Sensitivity analysis on an unclosed equation
inapplicable: Descriptive analyses making no prediction
positive_pattern: Restitution is measured on calibration impacts, then a frame-consistent momentum model predicts held-out exit speed while all recoil states and roots satisfy conservation and physical bounds.
procedure: Build a symbol table with units, point or frame, input or unknown status, and source.
Count independent equations and unknowns.
Draw the dependency graph and reject any path where the target output defines a parameter used to predict itself.
Separate calibration data from prediction cases.
Solve all physical roots and test bounds.
Substitute the solution back into every governing equation.
Check limiting cases, conservation, and identifiability.
Expose unresolved parameters as scenarios rather than hidden constants.
statement: Require every predictive physical model to have a noncircular algebraic closure: all variables defined, independent inputs measured or justified, unknown count matched by compatible equations, and outputs excluded from their own calibration path.

forbidden: Accessibility used to excuse undefined variables or invalid conservation
Decorative domain prose that delays the task
Equations without physical interpretation
Simple diagrams presented as validation
Audience confidence substituted for uncertainty
Policy rhetoric stronger than the model
inapplicable: Formal specialist derivations where no broader audience is required
positive_pattern: A baseball-facing report separates tactile and performance sweet spots, illustrates center-of-percussion mechanics, escalates to an optimizer, presents scenario graphs, and closes against clarity, applicability, and resiliency criteria while preserving rigorous caveats.
procedure: Name the target reader and the decisions or questions they need answered.
Define ambiguous domain terms before modeling.
State technical and communication acceptance criteria.
Begin with a familiar baseline and explain exactly why it is insufficient.
Introduce one mechanism and equation block at a time.
Pair equations with minimal diagrams and physical-unit results.
Provide a contents map and stable visual grammar.
Return to the declared criteria in the conclusion.
Keep uncertainty, causal limits, and policy bridges explicit despite simplification.
statement: Design a technical competition paper around an explicit audience contract, using layered definitions, a simple baseline, mechanism diagrams, unit-bearing results, and deeper mathematics without weakening evidence standards.

applicability: Tracks, ramps, half-pipes, slides, and passive transport paths
Shape optimization with human or vehicle motion
forbidden: Changing depth while calling the result a pure shape effect
A zero-height or zero-width optimum
Infinitesimal-radius turns with no load bound
A symmetric curve that violates midpoint slope continuity
Ignoring initial speed in a path derivation
Calling a cross-section reduction lossless without a coupling bound
Replacing practical design with an unconstrained asymptote
inapplicable: Pure mathematical path problems where physical feasibility is explicitly outside scope
positive_pattern: A spline or clothoid half-pipe is optimized at common width and depth with coping-angle, curvature, g-load, contact, buildability, and snow-volume bounds; feasible vertical-air and rotation tradeoffs are reported with uncertainty.
procedure: Define each performance objective in physical units and separate energy, time, comfort, safety, and spectacle.
Choose a geometry representation that can satisfy all endpoint and symmetry conditions.
Hold width, depth, arc length, footprint, or material budget fixed according to the estimand.
Enforce tangent, curvature, curvature-rate, contact, peak-load, construction, and minimum-feature constraints.
Include initial speed, gravity, dissipation, active input, and three-dimensional coupling required by the claim.
Solve every candidate with stopping and contact-loss events.
Check analytic limits and matched counterfactuals.
Report feasible optima, tolerances, uncertainty, and Pareto alternatives rather than a degenerate boundary limit.
statement: Optimize a physical path only over a nondegenerate, matched, and buildable geometry set, while solving the full motion and enforcing endpoint, smoothness, contact, load, safety, and construction constraints.

applicability: Vehicle and body motion on constrained paths
forbidden: Calling curvature-dependent Coulomb loss aerodynamic drag
One coefficient for snow and air without calibration
Negative kinetic energy treated as an exit state
No contact-loss event
A force diagram whose declared angle disagrees with its components
No-loss-of-generality claims for omitted slope without a bound
inapplicable: Ideal conservative baselines that explicitly make no dissipative prediction
positive_pattern: A rider model uses mu_s N for snow, one-half rho C_D A v_rel squared for air, measured pumping work, and explicit stop/contact events, then validates speed and airtime on held-out runs.
procedure: Draw the full force diagram in a declared coordinate system.
Write snow or surface friction from calibrated contact mechanics and normal load.
Write aerodynamic drag from relative air speed, density, projected area, and drag coefficient.
Add rolling, plowing, deformation, and active-work terms only when relevant.
Calibrate mechanisms separately under matched conditions.
Propagate them through one energy or state equation with consistent signs and units.
Stop integration at zero kinetic energy or contact loss.
Validate force, speed, energy, and event location against measured trajectories.
Test slope and three-dimensional coupling before claiming dimensional reduction.
statement: Model each dissipative mechanism with its own force law, geometry, units, calibration data, and validity regime; do not merge surface friction, aerodynamic drag, plowing, and active human work because they share a speed exponent.

applicability: Snowboard, diving, gymnastics, skating, and other aerial-sport design
forbidden: Assuming internal motion cannot change angular velocity
Rotation count equal to airtime divided by one universal period
Pumping described without an impulse or trajectory model
Two athletes used as causal evidence
Landing farther inside assumed better without load and success analysis
An angle formula that fails at zero deviation
inapplicable: Rigid projectiles with no orientation or landing requirement
positive_pattern: Tracked runs calibrate takeoff impulse and posture schedules; simulation predicts trajectory, accumulated rotation, opening margin, landing point, and landing load across athlete scenarios.
procedure: Define vertical air, total airtime, twist, flip, landing location, and successful landing separately.
Estimate takeoff linear and angular impulse from athlete-surface interaction.
Propagate the center-of-mass trajectory in the actual course geometry.
Conserve total angular momentum during flight while allowing posture-dependent inertia and coupled body axes.
Reserve time and orientation margin for opening and landing.
Intersect the trajectory with the course surface and check impact speed, angle, and load.
Represent athlete skill and strategy distributions.
Validate against tracked multi-athlete, multi-run kinematics.
Optimize a feasible rotation probability or risk-adjusted score rather than airtime alone.
statement: Model aerial rotation as a coupled takeoff, flight, body-configuration, and landing-feasibility problem, preserving linear and angular impulse, time-varying inertia, trajectory-surface intersection, and skill uncertainty.

forbidden: Speed in the caption and kinetic energy on the axis
Different axis ranges used as if directly comparable
Candidate curves with hidden differences in depth or width
Negative physical states plotted without infeasibility labels
A plot ranking designs without the constraints that generated them
No uncertainty or convergence indication
inapplicable: A single design with no comparator or decision
positive_pattern: Aligned half-pipe profiles list common width and depth, speed and normal-load trajectories share units, stopping points are marked, and a Pareto table links each buildable design to vertical air, rotation, risk, and cost.
procedure: Show candidate geometries on common coordinates and scale.
Annotate width, depth, arc length, endpoint angle, curvature limit, and fixed versus varied quantities.
Plot response against a common physical coordinate or normalized progress with shared limits where comparison is intended.
Mark zero-energy, contact-loss, load-limit, and infeasible regions.
Use consistent metric names and units in captions, axes, prose, and tables.
Add uncertainty or convergence bands.
Pair results with a table of objectives, constraints, outputs, and feasibility.
Show selected Pareto designs as linked thumbnails.
statement: Compare candidate physical designs with aligned geometry views, common constraints, unit-bearing response trajectories, feasibility events, uncertainty, and a compact decision table that makes unmatched assumptions impossible to miss.

forbidden: Uninitialized state read by a loop or derivative
A declared force parameter unused by the solver
Independent if blocks that overwrite a geometry branch
A derivative variable unset on part of the domain
Paper equations with different units from code
Dead residual computation
Smaller time step claimed to validate broken derivatives
Tables produced by an unidentified code variant
inapplicable: Pure analytic work with no executable implementation
positive_pattern: One tested solver initializes all six states, evaluates a branch-complete curve object, keeps the body on the surface, applies vector drag and friction, uses calibrated pumping, passes energy and nested-model tests, converges under refinement, and reproduces every paper result.
procedure: Map each paper symbol and equation to one typed code variable and derivative.
Initialize every state and local variable on every control-flow path.
Implement piecewise geometry through one total function that returns position, tangent, and curvature consistently.
Compile with maximum warnings and run static analysis, sanitizers, and undefined-behavior checks.
Detect unused parameters, dead computations, shadowed assignments, and unreachable branches.
Add unit, sign, conservation, constraint-residual, event, and limiting-case tests.
Verify that active inputs such as work or pumping change the expected state and that zero inputs recover the baseline.
Perform time-step and tolerance convergence only after structural tests pass.
Regenerate every table, percentage, figure, and prose claim from the tested executable.
statement: Treat executable physical-model code as a second formal specification: initialize every state, make geometry branches total, connect every declared parameter, preserve equation-code-unit parity, and test invariants, events, constraints, and outputs before trusting numerical accuracy.

forbidden: A constant pumping force with no timing or calibration
Work added without division by mass in a speed equation
A force parameter declared but unused in code
Horizontal launch described without trajectory equations
Airtime assumed to determine rotation at fixed universal rate
Unmodeled conversion of downhill speed used to select a practical design
inapplicable: Passive-object baselines that explicitly exclude athlete actuation
positive_pattern: Measured stance-phase force and posture drive a bounded work and angular-impulse model whose no-pump limit recovers passive motion and whose takeoff speed, rotation, and landing predictions validate on held-out runs.
procedure: Define the exact performance pathway from athlete action to takeoff linear and angular state.
Choose force, power, impulse, or work as the actuation variable and keep units consistent.
Specify direction in the local tangent-normal frame and contact phase or timing.
Impose biomechanical magnitude, duration, posture, fatigue, and skill bounds.
Integrate work and impulse into the same translational and rotational dynamics as gravity, contact, and dissipation.
Calibrate against force, inertial, or tracked kinematic data across athletes and runs.
Ablate pumping to recover the passive baseline and verify that every actuation parameter affects the intended state.
Propagate takeoff changes through flight, rotation, landing, and risk.
Report strategy and athlete uncertainty rather than one universal force.
statement: Model athlete pumping as a calibrated, bounded, phase-dependent exchange of force, power, and angular impulse with the course, coupled to posture, contact, trajectory, fatigue, and landing rather than as a qualitative story or constant disconnected input.

forbidden: Calling an imposed upper bound an optimized interior value
Using bisection on a nonmonotone multivariable objective without a bracketed scalar root
Reporting a small integration step without a convergence study
Fixing an event location that the design itself should determine
Reporting spline-intersection precision without data or interpolation error
Using one nominal optimum when plausible uncertainty reverses the decision
inapplicable: Purely descriptive parameter sweeps that make no optimality claim
positive_pattern: A constrained half-pipe optimizer maximizes simulated vertical air over buildable splines, endogenizes flight and landing, labels an active height bound, agrees across refined solvers and multistart algorithms, and reports a stable near-optimal Pareto set.
procedure: State the physical objective in units and distinguish it from every proxy.
Declare all decision variables, bounds, equality and inequality constraints, fixed quantities, and event definitions.
Plot or otherwise inspect the feasible response before choosing an optimizer.
Choose an algorithm whose monotonicity, differentiability, convexity, or bracketing requirements are satisfied.
Document initialization, tolerances, termination, infeasible handling, and all searched roots or starts.
Separate interior stationary points from active-bound and degenerate solutions.
Verify state-solver, mesh or step, interpolation, and optimizer convergence independently.
Compare analytic special cases and alternative algorithms or multistart results.
Propagate parameter and model uncertainty through the optimizer and report recommendation reversals or near-optimal sets.
Publish enough code, data, and traces to regenerate the selected design and decision figures.
statement: Treat every numerical optimum as a reproducible claim: define the estimand and feasible set, use an algorithm whose assumptions match the objective, classify boundary solutions, demonstrate solver and discretization convergence, and test recommendation stability under uncertainty.

applicability: Physical designs with competing performance objectives
forbidden: Normalizing regression coefficients that carry different units
Treating predictive coefficients as preference weights without justification
Averaging independently optimized design coordinates
Calling a score-only solution practical
Hiding normalization baselines or value-function shapes
Reporting one compromise without Pareto or preference sensitivity
inapplicable: Single-objective optimization with one dimensionally coherent response

judge_relevance.basis: The paper is a Finalist, but no judge commentary attributes award outcomes to its tradeoff formulation.

positive_pattern: A course-design study computes vertical air, rotation, landing load, and cost on one feasible geometry set, presents the Pareto frontier, and selects a design only after applying dimensionless stakeholder value functions with sensitivity analysis.
procedure: Write every objective with its unit, direction, baseline, and valid domain.
Separate predictive coefficients from stakeholder preferences.
Normalize objective values through explicit dimensionless value functions or preserve them as a Pareto vector.
Include safety, feasibility, construction, and other practical constraints before calling the design practical.
Optimize the combined utility directly over the shared decision variables or compute the Pareto frontier.
Compare the selected compromise with each single-objective optimum and nearby nondominated alternatives.
Vary normalization, preference weights, regression uncertainty, and constraints to identify recommendation reversals.
Report the chosen tradeoff and the preference assumptions that make it appropriate.
statement: Optimize multi-objective physical designs in a unit-consistent utility or Pareto space; do not normalize regression coefficients with incompatible units into preference weights or replace the combined optimization with a weighted average of separate argmax locations.

applicability: Hybrid pipelines combining cell, component, structure, and system models
Problem A papers with dependent submodels
forbidden: Using a section sequence as evidence of coupling
Passing a proxy into a later equation without a unit conversion
Aggregating cell or leaf outputs to a tree with an unnamed sum or coefficient
Borrowing separately calibrated submodels without interface recalibration
Calling an infeasible branch part of the final integrated model
Hiding interface uncertainty inside free coefficients
inapplicable: Independent models intentionally reported as separate alternatives with no shared conclusion

judge_relevance.basis: The paper is an Outstanding Winner, but no judge commentary attributes the award to its multiscale architecture or interface quality.

positive_pattern: A leaf-to-tree model maps measured cell flux to leaf transport, aggregates calibrated leaf flows to branches, converts branch outputs into tree-scale energy with compatible units, and passes interface and end-to-end holdout tests.
procedure: Draw the model dependency graph before writing equations.
For every edge, name the exact output symbol and receiving input symbol.
Align units, reference frames, spatial support, temporal support, and population or component scope.
Define the aggregation, reduction, or interpolation operator explicitly.
Calibrate interface coefficients independently from the final target.
Propagate uncertainty and covariance across the edge.
Test each interface with synthetic recovery, limiting cases, and held-out component data.
Run end-to-end perturbations and report which downstream decisions change.
If an interface cannot be closed, label the models as alternatives or retire that branch rather than implying integration.
statement: For every component-to-interaction-to-system model pipeline, define a typed interface contract for each handoff: variable, physical meaning, unit, spatial and temporal support, aggregation rule, uncertainty, calibration source, and interface validation; a verbal sequence of scales is not model coupling.

applicability: Problem A tasks that classify physical shapes, images, contours, or structures from engineered descriptors
Prototype, nearest-distance, AHP-weighted, or small-reference-set classifiers
forbidden: Calling AHP consistency predictive validation
Testing only the example used to select the expected class
Ignoring within-class dispersion
Forcing every object into a closed prototype list
Claiming robustness without preprocessing perturbations or independent labels
Selecting visually similar pairs and then treating regression p-values as independent evidence
inapplicable: Tasks with no labeled decision target or where a continuous physical estimator is required instead of classification

judge_relevance.basis: The paper is an Outstanding Winner, but no judge commentary attributes the award to its image-classification choices.

positive_pattern: A calibrated contour pipeline produces invariant descriptors, estimates class distributions from training data, retains an unknown-class option, and reports ablation and holdout confusion results with uncertainty.
procedure: Define the deployment classes and an unknown or reject option.
Calibrate image scale, orientation, segmentation, and contour extraction.
Choose descriptors from mechanism or training evidence and test scale, rotation, and acquisition invariance.
Estimate class distributions rather than storing only one prototype.
Learn or justify feature scaling and weights without using the holdout labels.
Test feature ablations and compare with simple baselines.
Evaluate on an independent labeled holdout with confusion matrix, classwise error, uncertainty, and sensitivity to preprocessing.
Separate judgment consistency checks from predictive performance claims.
statement: Build interpretable image-based classifiers from calibrated and invariant measurements, and separate feature-weight coherence from predictive validity: represent within-class variation and unknown classes, justify or learn weights on training data, and evaluate ablations and uncertainty on independent labeled holdouts.
